- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is trending up, cap the rise at 2–3% above recent mean to avoid false momentum.  
- After a strong upward move in price, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast to allow a 1–2 day lagged dip before rebound.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8) and forecast is noisy, smooth the 30-day curve by averaging 5–7 day windows to reduce overfitting.  
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion bias: next forecast = prior + 0.5×(true - forecast) to avoid runaway inflation.  
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price is flat or declining, reduce forecast slope by 15–20% to account for sentiment-driven overvaluation.
